transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. That pattern points firmly at the brush drive rather than the main motor. Good suction through the hose means the suction motor is working; it's the spinning brush that does the carpet pickup. A burning rubber smell just before it stopped is a common sign of the rubber drive belt slipping and overheating, usually because the brush bar got jammed, often with hair or thread. The belt then snaps or stretches and the brush stops turning. Because there was a burning smell, please don't use it again until a qualified engineer has checked it. You can still do a couple of looks with it unplugged to narrow it down: 1. Unplug it, turn the floorhead over and look at the brush bar. Cut away any hair or thread wrapped round it and at the end caps (scissors along the groove work well), then see if it turns freely by hand. If it was badly tangled or stiff, that's very likely what caused the belt to burn. If it's broken or still won't turn, the bar or its bearings may be seized.
2. Still unplugged, look at the belt. On most corded uprights it sits under the base plate, which usually unclips or has a few screws. If it's snapped, stretched, glazed or off its pulley, that's the cause of the stopped brush. If it's intact and tight and the bar turns freely, the brush motor or its cut-out is more likely. Let me know what you find under there, as that will tell an engineer, or me, exactly where to look.

ok unplugged n turned it over. bar turns but tight, loads of hair n a bit of tassel wrapped round the ends. cut it all off n now it spins free by hand. belt is snapped in 2 bits, one bit has a shiny melted looking edge

⚠ Stop using this appliance
That's a very clear picture, and it fits the usual pattern. The hair and tassel wound round the ends made the brush bar stiff. The motor kept turning, so the belt slipped on the pulley and got hot. That caused the burning rubber smell and the shiny melted edge, until the belt finally snapped. Suction through the hose is fine, so the main motor isn't the problem. I'm fairly confident the snapped drive belt, caused by the jammed brush bar, is the whole story here. Because there was a burning smell, it still needs a qualified engineer to check it before it's used again. A few more looks with it unplugged will tell them, and you, whether anything else got cooked. 1. Look at the small metal spindle on the motor where the belt loops on, and inside the belt channel. If there's melted black rubber stuck to the spindle, it'll need cleaning off before any new belt can grip properly. If it's clean, good.
2. Check the base plate, the belt area and the brush bar end caps for scorched, browned or warped plastic. If you find only melted belt, that points to a straightforward belt job. If plastic is scorched or deformed, the heat went further and the engineer should look closely at the floorhead and motor.
3. Spin the brush bar again and feel the ends. If it turns smoothly with no grinding, roughness or wobble, the bearings have probably survived. If it's gritty or wobbly, the bar or its end caps may be worn too. If everything apart from the belt looks undamaged, it's usually a simple, inexpensive repair. To stop it happening again, cut hair off the brush bar every few weeks, and switch off straight away if you ever smell rubber again. Can you tell me what you see on those points, and whether the smell seemed to come from the floorhead or the main body?
bar spins smooth now, no wobble or grinding. didnt see any scorched plastic but not sure about the motor spindle bit. smell was only right when it stopped, gone now. so just need a new belt?

[Heading: Likely cause: drive belt (snapped or stretched)]
Yes, probably a new drive belt is all it needs. The bar was jammed with hair, the belt slipped and melted, then it snapped. The bar now spins smoothly, there's no scorched plastic, suction is fine and the smell stopped when the belt went. That tells me the heat stayed in the belt and didn't reach the motor or wiring. 1. Get the right belt by checking the model number on the rating label. It's usually on the back or underneath the main body. Vax belts vary between models, so match it to that rather than guessing.
2. Before fitting, unplug it and look closely at the small metal motor spindle where the belt loops on. If there's any black melted rubber stuck to it, pick and wipe it off. A cloth with a little washing-up liquid, or a fingernail, works well. If you leave it on, the new belt can slip and wear quickly.
3. If you smell burning again, or the main body gets hot or sounds wrong, switch off straight away. In that case, have a repair shop look at the motor. With a clean bar and a fresh belt, though, I'd expect it to be back to normal. To stop it happening again, turn the head over every few weeks and snip off any hair wrapping round the bar. Do it sooner if you have long hair, pets or tasselled rugs. Is there anything else I can help with?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
model number on the back sticker says U85-AS-Be. do u know what belt that takes?

[Heading: Likely cause: drive belt (snapped or stretched)]
I can't safely tell you the exact belt, because I can't confirm part fit for a specific model. Vax uprights use several different belts that look alike but differ in length and width, and the wrong one will slip or burn again. 1. Enter U85-AS-Be on Vax's official spares and support site, or give it to a reputable vacuum parts supplier. Either should list the belt that fits it.
2. Keep the two snapped pieces. Laying them end to end next to the new belt lets you check the length, width and profile (flat or ribbed) match before you fit it.
3. Belts are often sold in packs of two, so it's handy to have a spare. After that, it should be back to picking up nicely. The best way to stop it happening again is to turn the head over every few weeks and snip off any hair or tassel threads before they build up. Is there anything else I can help with?
